_source: bina-gtm/notes/ESA_State_Database.xlsx — the bina team's ESA database. Sync this file from it; do not invent numbers.

programs.who: Any Alabama K–12 family — the program is opening up in phases.
programs.howMuch: $7,000 per child per year at a participating school ($2,000 if homeschooling, capped at $4,000 per family).
programs.window: Applications open each spring — one window per year.

programs.who: Every Arizona K–12 family — no income or special-needs requirement.
programs.howMuch: $7,000–$8,000 per child per year (up to $25,000–$30,000+ for kids with special needs).
programs.window: Any time — applications are open year-round and approval takes about 30 days.
programs.docs: You'll need a birth certificate, proof you live in Arizona, and a signed contract (plus IEP/diagnosis documents for special-needs awards).
programs.boost: Arizona's handbook explicitly approves “tuition or fees for a nonpublic online learning program” — exactly the category bina is in.

programs.who: Every Arkansas K–12 family.
programs.howMuch: About $6,900–$7,600 per child per year.
programs.window: Apply between March 9 and June 1 — complete it by June 1 to secure your child's spot.

programs.who: Every Florida family (much higher amounts for kids with special needs).
programs.howMuch: About $8,200 per child per year on average (up to $22,000–$34,000 for some special-needs cases).
programs.window: Applications open in cycles throughout the year.

programs.who: Families under the income limit whose child is zoned for certain public schools.
programs.howMuch: $6,500 per child per year.
programs.window: The portal re-opens each application period — check mygeorgiapromise.org for the current window.

programs.who: Full-time nonpublic or homeschooled students ages 5–19 (up to 22 with disabilities); lower incomes get priority.
programs.howMuch: Up to $5,000 per child per year ($7,500 for kids with special needs) — paid as a tax credit or advance payment.
programs.window: Two application windows a year (the 2026 spring window ran Jan 15 – Mar 15; the next is expected summer/fall).

programs.who: Kids with a qualifying disability (and their siblings).
programs.howMuch: Up to $8,000 per child per year (up to $20,000 for special needs).

programs.who: Every Iowa K–12 family — no income limits.
programs.howMuch: $8,148 per child per year.

programs.who: Lower-income families, through approved scholarship organizations.
programs.howMuch: Up to $8,000 per child per year.

programs.who: Families under the income cap and kids with qualifying disabilities get priority.
programs.howMuch: $7,626 per child per year for families under the income cap (up to $15,253 for qualifying disabilities).

programs.who: Kids with a qualifying special-education need.
programs.howMuch: About $8,000 per child per year.

programs.who: Lower-income families and kids with disabilities get priority.
programs.howMuch: Varies — up to about $11,800 for kids with special needs.

programs.who: Kids with special needs — but the program is paused right now.
programs.howMuch: $5,000–$8,000 per child per year (varies by district).
programs.window: On hold — verify before planning around it.
programs.special: This program is paused by a lawsuit. Current students receive reimbursements through June 30, 2026; new enrollment is uncertain.

programs.who: Families under the state income limit (the program has a 10,000-student cap).
programs.howMuch: About $4,800–$5,200 per child per year.
programs.window: One application window a year — apply early because of the student cap.
programs.payNote: Funds arrive in four installments through the year (September, November, January, April).

programs.who: Kids with a qualifying disability (ESA+); most families through the Opportunity Scholarship.
programs.howMuch: ESA+: $9,000 per child per year (up to $17,000 for special needs). Opportunity Scholarship: about $3,600–$7,900.

programs.who: Every Ohio family — the amount scales with income.
programs.howMuch: $6,166 per child per year for K–8 ($8,408 for grades 9–12).

programs.who: Every family — the credit amount depends on your income.
programs.howMuch: $5,000–$7,500 per child per year, depending on income.

programs.who: Families under the income limit — the limit rises each year.
programs.howMuch: $7,634 per child per year.

programs.who: Most families — the program is opening up statewide.
programs.howMuch: $7,530 per child per year.

programs.who: Every Texas family.
programs.howMuch: $10,474 per child for the 2026–27 school year.
programs.window: Applications open February 4 and close March 17.

programs.who: Every Utah K–12 family — but demand exceeds funds, so not everyone who applies gets an award.
programs.howMuch: $8,000 per child per year on the private-school track ($4,000–$6,000 homeschool).
programs.window: One window a year — the 2026–27 window closed May 1; apply the day the next one opens.
programs.special: A court appeal is pending; the program continues during the appeal. Awards aren't guaranteed — apply as early as possible.

programs.who: Most families — it's designed for kids leaving public school or just starting school.
programs.howMuch: About $5,400 per child per year.
programs.payNote: Funds arrive in two halves — by August 15 and mid-year.

programs.who: Families under the program income limits.
programs.howMuch: $10,877 per child per year for K–8 ($13,371 for grades 9–12).

programs.who: Most Wyoming families.
programs.howMuch: $7,000 per child per year.
programs.window: Applications open in early July for a few weeks (2026: from July 6) — returning families renew with pre-filled forms.
